observations.body: Priscilla and Aquila instruct Apollos. Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures. for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

payload.posture: Read Acts 18:24–28 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states priscilla and Aquila instruct Apollos. Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures. for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
